questions.a: Lakshadweep is 36 coral islands in the Arabian Sea; the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are more than 500 volcanic islands in the Bay of Bengal. Asha wrongly makes both volcanic and puts both in the Bay of Bengal.
o: Only Bilal's
Only Asha's
Both are right
Neither, because Bilal has swapped the two seas

questions.q: A student says, 'Lakshadweep's uninhabited coral islands are useless to India.' (a) What does the chapter say India controls because of Lakshadweep? (b) Name the three purposes it allows.
questions.a: (a) A vast marine area. (b) Fishing, resource exploration and environmental protection.
s: Part (a): a vast marine area
Part (b): fishing, resource exploration and environmental protection

questions.q: 'India's coasts and islands give it ports, farmland and a presence in the ocean.' Justify this statement using the west coast, the east coast, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
questions.a: West coast: important ports and cities, centres of economic activity for millennia, and Mumbai, the financial centre. East coast: wide plains and deltas such as the Godavari and Krishna whose fertile land is ideal for farming. Lakshadweep: India controls a vast marine area, allowing fishing, resource exploration and environmental protection. Andaman and Nicobar: more than 500 volcanic islands whose location is very important, like outposts keeping an eye on the ocean. Together they show the coasts and islands matter for trade, food and India's reach into the sea.
s: West coast ports and cities
East coast deltas and farming
Lakshadweep's marine area
Andaman and Nicobar's important location
Concludes with trade, food and reach into the ocean

questions.q: Lakshadweep is made up of 36 coral islands, and not all of them are inhabited. If 11 are inhabited, the number of uninhabited islands is ___.
A pamphlet says, 'Lakshadweep has several active volcanoes on its coral islands, and Barren Island is only one of them.' Show using the chapter that this cannot be right.
questions.a: The chapter says Lakshadweep is made of 36 coral islands in the Arabian Sea. Barren Island lies in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal, and it is the only active volcano in India, so there cannot be several active volcanoes.
s: Lakshadweep consists of coral islands, not volcanoes
Barren Island is in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
It is the only active volcano in India, so 'several' is impossible

questions.q: An environment journal says, 'The Sundarbans are India's own mangrove delta.' (a) Correct it with the chapter's fact about the delta's location. (b) Give two features of the delta that the chapter names.
questions.a: (a) The Sundarbans lie in the delta of the Ganga, the Brahmaputra and their tributaries; about half of it is in India and the rest in Bangladesh. (b) Any two of: a unique combination of river, sea and land; mangroves; many species including the Royal Bengal Tiger; a UNESCO Heritage site.
s: Part (a): about half in India and the rest in Bangladesh
Part (b): two valid features

questions.q: A teacher wants students to link cause and effect for the hills of the Northeast. (a) Which plateau do the Garo, Khasi and Jantia hills belong to? (b) Which feature of the climate does the chapter link to the region's forests, wildlife and fertile land?
questions.a: (a) The Meghalaya Plateau. (b) Its heavy rainfall, one of the highest in the world.
s: Part (a): the Meghalaya Plateau
Part (b): very heavy rainfall

questions.q:
A village council in the East Khasi Hills must provide a safe crossing over a stream in a region of very heavy rainfall before the next monsoon, six months away. Option A is a concrete bridge. Option B is a bridge of living tree roots, like those in neighbouring villages. The council also has a small heritage fund.
(a) Which plateau do the Khasi hills belong to?
(b) What does the chapter say living root bridges show about the tribes of the Northeast?
(c) How are such bridges made, and how long does it take?
(d) With a six-month deadline, which option should the council use for the crossing, and what could it do with the heritage fund?
questions.a: (a) The Meghalaya Plateau. (b) They show the craftsmanship of the tribes of the Northeast. (c) Tree roots are woven together over the course of many years. (d) Build the concrete bridge for the monsoon, since a root bridge takes many years; use the heritage fund to start growing a root bridge nearby, keeping the tribal craft and attracting visitors.
s: Part (a): Meghalaya Plateau
Part (b): craftsmanship of the tribes
Part (c): weaving tree roots over many years
Part (d): concrete bridge now, root bridge started as heritage

questions.q: The Sundarbans are described as a delta with 'a unique combination of the river, sea and land'. Justify this description with four points from the chapter.
questions.a: The Sundarbans lie in the delta of the Ganga, Brahmaputra and their tributaries, where river, sea and land meet. About half is in India and the rest in Bangladesh. Mangroves grow in the delta. It is home to many species, including the Royal Bengal Tiger. It is a UNESCO Heritage site.
s: Location in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta where river, sea and land meet
Shared between India and Bangladesh
Mangroves of the delta
Wildlife such as the Royal Bengal Tiger
UNESCO Heritage site, concluding the description is justified
